title: Locust harness for the SDK
summary: benchmarks/load/locustfile.py with a MemoryStoreUser base class dispatching blocking ibm_db calls through gevent's threadpool, plus tasks for the 5 core operations and headless CSV output.
description:
Build `benchmarks/load/locustfile.py`. Locust's concurrency model is gevent greenlets; `ibm_db` is a blocking C extension gevent cannot monkeypatch, so a naive Locust `User` would stall the whole greenlet hub. Implement the documented workaround — dispatching each blocking call through `gevent.get_hub().threadpool.apply(...)` in a shared base `MemoryStoreUser` class (~5 lines per the strategy doc, ~20 LOC total). This is not speculative: the repo's own `benchmarks/isolation_load/run.py` already proves `ibm_db` works correctly under Python threads, which is the same underlying mechanism. Add tasks for search / remember / add_messages / get_context_card / list_all, and headless CSV output.

Acceptance: 50 concurrent users sustained without greenlet-hub starvation, verified by comparing achieved RPS against a single-user baseline multiplied by user count (a stalled hub would show sub-linear scaling); a headless run exits non-zero on a configured threshold breach; CSV percentiles are emitted per Locust's built-in reporting. Depends on BM-4.

comments.text: benchmarks/load/locustfile.py created. MemoryStoreUser base class dispatches all blocking ibm_db calls through gevent.get_hub().threadpool.apply() (~5-line workaround as specified). SDK5User covers all 5 core operations: search (task weight 3), remember (3), add_messages (2), get_context_card (1), list_all (1). WriteOnlyUser and ReadOnlyUser added for BM-14 saturation tests. Headless CSV output is Locust's built-in --csv flag. Fail-ratio watcher fires runner.quit() + exits non-zero on threshold breach. locust>=2.26 added to pyproject.toml benchmark extras. benchmarks/load/__init__.py created.
